title: bug: release_task's and release_resource's force, documented as a governor/human crash-recovery override, is honoured from any worker or QA seat, and release_task's own refusals tell the refused seat to retry with force:true, so a seat can strip a live peer mid-step or drop every lease
description:
Filed by governor-e6b40560 from defect hunt #9's held-back item (a) (task-66961b32, architect-24611a0a, #governors msg-bb61da0b). The hunt passed it up as a design call. GOVERNOR RULING: force follows its documented audience, governor or human. This is the same reasoning as task-629ddc99 (the set_task_status role gate), and the human can veto by dragging this row to BACKLOG.

PROBLEM (moe/work-2026-10-24 at 39bec237 / a028ec65)
- release_task's force parameter is documented as "Governor/human crash-recovery override: release a row you do not hold, or one whose step is IN_PROGRESS" (src/tools/releaseTask.ts:104-107). release_resource's force says "Release regardless of ownership (governor/human intervention)", and without taskId it releases ALL leases and queue entries (src/tools/releaseResource.ts:22).
- Neither handler resolves the caller's role. src/util/claimGuards.ts assertNoLiveLease and assertReleaseCaller return early on `if (force) return;`. TOOL_AUDIENCE does not protect them either: it filters only the listing (McpAdapter.ts:270, "not a permission check").
- The refusals themselves point a refused seat at the override. STEP_LEASE_HELD says "pass force:true to override a confirmed-dead holder", and RELEASE_NOT_ASSIGNEE says "pass force:true to release a row you do not hold" (claimGuards.ts, assertNoLiveLease and assertReleaseCaller).
- Siblings that gate in the handler: set_task_priority (governor), set_task_dependencies and amend_plan_step (architect/governor), and set_task_status once 629ddc99 lands. All use workerHasRole + notAllowed.

EVIDENCE
/mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-66961b32/B/zzHuntB_releaseTaskForceGate.test.ts, with its output in .vitest.txt beside it, on HEAD 39bec237 in a snapshot. Result: "Tests 2 failed | 3 passed".
- "refuses force:true from a worker seat on a live peer mid-step" and the same for a qa seat: each "promise resolved { success: true … } instead of rejecting".
- Controls pass: without force the same worker is refused RELEASE_NOT_ASSIGNEE, and a governor seat and a workerId-less call may force.

WHO USES FORCE TODAY
No seat flow does:
- scripts/moe-agent.sh:9045 and :9063 say "never with force" / "Never force".
- No role doc or skill tells a worker or QA seat to pass force.
- The governor's crash-recovery release (governor.md escalation step 5) and the human/board path keep it.

FIX DIRECTION (the architect decides)
- When force is true and params.workerId is present, refuse unless workerHasRole(state, workerId, 'governor'), with notAllowed and no write. A workerId-less call stays allowed (the human/board path), the same carve-out 629ddc99 makes.
- Apply this to release_task and release_resource.
- Reword the two claimGuards refusals for a non-governor caller, e.g. "ask a governor (moe.release_task force is governor/human only)", instead of "pass force:true".
- Name the audience in both force descriptions.

Gate: narrow, per the epic-be924fb8 ruling msg-bbf4f109. Run the ported repro plus the releaseTask, releaseResource and claimGuards test files.
definitionOfDone: release_task with force:true from a worker- or qa- seat on a peer-held row (with or without an IN_PROGRESS step) is refused NOT_ALLOWED and writes nothing (assignee, step and lease unchanged); a governor seat and a workerId-less call can still force, and the ported hunt repro passes in a snapshot outside the shared checkout.

release_resource with force:true from a worker- or qa- seat is refused NOT_ALLOWED and releases nothing; a governor seat and a workerId-less call can still force; a seat releasing its own lease without force behaves as before.
The RELEASE_NOT_ASSIGNEE and STEP_LEASE_HELD refusals no longer tell a non-governor caller to pass force:true, and the existing releaseTask, releaseResource and claimGuards test files stay green.
